court: High Court of Judicature at Bombay
case_name: Aakash Shrikant Sanas And 4 Others vs State Of Mah. Thr. Pso Ps Pardi Nagpur

parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Aakash Shrikant Sanas (Husband), Sagar Shrikant Sanas (Brother-in-law), Yogita Shrikant Sanas (Sister-in-law), Manohar Sahadev Shinde (Maternal Uncle), Anuradha Shrikant Sanas (Mother-in-law)
parties.respondent_defendant: State of Maharashtra, Through Police Station Officer, Police Station Pardi, Nagpur

facts_of_case: The applicants prayed for quashment of the F.I.R. No. 552/2021 registered with the Police Station Pardi, Nagpur for the offences punishable under Sections 498-A, 323, 504, 506 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the applicant to establish that the FIR is frivolous and that there are no reasonable grounds for proceeding with the prosecution.
legal_principles.held: It is also pointed out to the Court by her as well as the Applicant No. 1 that they have filed the Petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act for dissolution of marriage by mutual consent which is pending in the Court of learned Judge, Family Court, Nagpur.

legal_principles.principle: A complainant's willingness to withdraw the complaint and not prosecute it is a relevant factor in considering whether the FIR should be quashed.
legal_principles.held: On the query from the Court, she submitted that there is no pressure on her for withdrawal of the First Information Report and the Final Report.

outcome.final_order: Rule is made returnable forthwith. Heard finally by consent of the parties.
